thread:
maya: FYI customer (AcmeHealth) reported repeated p99 spikes during 4k+ context inference bursts this afternoon. PM asked for a clear fallback + prefetch story we can promise in contract.
li: Can you paste the logs/snips? is this CPU fallback or routing to other model variants?
maya: Logs attached in ticket — main pattern is GPU queue/backpressure causing large tail latencies. They want deterministic fallback to a quantized CPU kernel and prefetch of KV for repeated prefixes.
jamal: Quick thought: this is multi-dimensional — kernel selection, kv prefetch, routing policy, and rollout safety. We should write a short PRD: scope, acceptance criteria, rollout plan.
sophie: Product note: customer expects SLA wording around p99 and a documented fallback behavior. They also require audit logs of fallback events.
noah-pm: Priority is high for mid-market enterprise deals. If we can commit to a documented behavior (even if opt-in), it unlocks a deal.
oliver: From runtime side, we need at least these pieces scoped for an MVP:
- routing policy toggle: "gpu_preference: strict|best_effort|fallback"
- deterministic CPU fallback path with quantization profile mapping
- KV prefetch policy attached to route metadata (hint TTL, prefetch window)
- telemetry tag on requests that experienced fallback
jamal: Acceptance criteria proposal (MVP):
1) Functional: On GPU queue depth > 0.95 or per-request wait > X ms, requests are re-routed to quantized-cpu kernel within < 5ms decision time.
2) Quality: outputs on CPU fallback must match GPU baseline within a token-level divergence threshold (BLEU-like) <= 2% for customer prompt sets.
3) SLO: For 4k context under standard burst load (configurable QPS), p50 < 40ms, p95 < 180ms, p99 < 350ms for hosted tier when fallback is enabled.
4) Observability: fallback events are logged with reason code, request_id, and kernel_variant. Dashboards show fallback rate and latency delta.
5) Rollout: automated canary (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automated rollback on error rate > 0.5% or quality regression detected.
noah-pm: Those look reasonable. Product asks that rollout can be gated per-customer (Dedicated/customers) and opt-in boolean in customer config. Also need copy for security and compliance.
li: Edge cases to call out in spec: streaming responses mid-request where fallback would occur half-way through generation; KV cache warm vs cold (prefetch could waste cycles); model variants that lack exact quantization mapping.
jamal: For streaming case, two options: 1) disallow mid-stream fallback (failover only between requests) or 2) implement stateful mid-stream migration which is complex. Recommend option 1 for MVP and document behavior.
maya: Customer prefers no silent degradations. If fallback happens mid-stream, we should surface a status header and keep their app instances aware.
oliver: Prefetch policy proposal (config knobs):
- prefetch_hint_ttl: seconds
- prefix_cache_size: tokens
- aggressive_prefetch: bool (only for dedicated pools)
Example snippet: ```route:
  kernel_policy:
    fallback_threshold: 0.95
    fallback_target: quantized-cpu-v2
  kv_prefetch:
    prefetch_hint_ttl: 30
    aggressive_prefetch: false
```
li: Implementation checklist (rough):
- [ ] kernel variant mapping table + quant profiles
- [ ] routing decision path + unit tests for thresholds
- [ ] telemetry & dashboard panels for fallback rate/latency/quality
- [ ] config locking per-customer for Dedicated
- [ ] canary rollout automation + rollback hooks
sophie: Launch criteria from product POV:
- Security review complete
- Docs for behavior and opt-in config published
- Acceptance tests pass on internal smoke prompts and >= 3 customer-specific prompt sets
- SLA language drafted for legal
noah-pm: Timeline ask: can we aim for an opt-in beta in 8 weeks? Sales needs a statement of work by then.
jamal: Engineering estimate: baseline implementation + tests ~6w, canary infra + dashboards 2w, QA/bugfix 1-2w. So 9-10w realistically. Might compress with parallel work if we cut scope (no mid-stream fallback, no aggressive prefetch for hosted).
maya: Tradeoff decision: product wants earlier signal for sales. Proposal: ship "fallback only" opt-in for Dedicated customers first (less impact), delay prefetch aggressive optimizations to Q3.
oliver: Agree — Dedicated path reduces risk. For hosted we can offer a preview flag but keep opt-in for specific customers.
li: Edge acceptance tests to add to PRD:
- simulated GPU backpressure test where fallback triggers for 1000 requests and outputs are compared against baseline
- streaming failover test confirming we do not attempt mid-stream kernel switch
- KV prefetch hit-rate measurement within 1 hour window
maya: I'll draft the PRD + RFC for the routing path and prefetch config and link to this thread. Requesting volunteers for review: @li @jamal @oliver @sophie.
deploy-bot: canary job scheduled when RFC merged -> runs daily canary for 5% traffic (disabled by default). :robot_face: 
jamal: Thanks — I'll start a draft RFC today and post a brief design doc for review.
sophie: If we get a customer sign-off, legal will need the fallback behavior text ASAP.
maya: noted. tagging this thread as next-priority for runtime roadmap planning.
li: quick Q — do we need to add model-variant compatibility matrix to the RFC?
oliver: Yes, mapping table required. I'll pull quant profiles and list unsupported ops.
noah-pm: Great work team. Keep the PRD tight; sales needs a short customer-facing doc.
maya: ok will do. End of thread.
